text:
sam: Quick follow-up from the RFC thread — I sketched a 'mini-phased' batching idea overnight. TL;DR: create very short-lived phases (~2-10ms) that gather compatible requests, then hand off to the normal batcher. Goal: reduce 99.9th token latency for small interactive requests while still getting decent packing for throughput. Want feedback on how this would mesh with admission, KV-cache eviction, and preemption paths.
jia: Sounds interesting. What's the admission signal? Would mini-phases bypass the normal admission credits or be gated by them?
sam: Good q. Proposal: mini-phases take a lightweight lease token from a separate micro-reservoir that is replenished by the admission controller. They don't consume full slot credits; think of it as 'phase tickets' scoped to tiny latency windows. If tickets exhausted, fall back to regular queuing.
max: I worry about headroom accounting. If we create a parallel reservoir we risk subtle overcommit during spikes. How do we bound it per-tenant?
sam: Per-tenant soft cap + global backstop. Each tenant gets N micro-tickets proportional to their long-term slot usage. Reservoir auto-trims under load. Also an emergency global throttle if GPU saturation rises.
ogla: What about KV-cache coherence/eviction? Micro-phases will create on-accelerator work for requests that might need KV prefetching. We need a contract: micro-phase must declare whether it requires fresh KV state or can use cached prefixes.
sam: Agreed. My sketch: micro-phase participants annotate a hint bit: `prefetch_needed` true/false. If true, they join a separate micro-prefetch queue that preloads necessary keys (cheap path) before the batch executes; otherwise they join fastpath. Prefetch queue has lower concurrency.
jia: That implies ordering differences. If prefetch introduces delay, the micro-phase might stretch beyond the time budget and hurt tail. Should we let prefetch join a subsequent micro-phase instead of delaying current one?
sam: Option A: delay micro-phase until prefetch finishes (simpler correctness). Option B: fastpath executes without prefetch and we accept occasional cache-miss penalty. I lean B for interactive queries where 1-2 token extra cost is preferable to waiting tens of ms.
max: Also need to think about eviction signals. If a micro-phase runs and evicts KV entries mid-flight, downstream batches could see higher latency variance. We should add an eviction-awareness metric and consider scheduling eviction windows off the micro-phase hotpath.
ogla: +1. Maybe treat micro-phases as 'cache-sensitive' and avoid running aggressive eviction during their windows. Add an 'eviction_hold' hint to the eviction controller.
infra-bot: auto-note: micro-reservoir metrics requested: 'micro_tickets_alloc', 'micro_tickets_used', 'micro_ticket_wait_ms', 'micro_phase_success_rate'.
jia: Rollout plan idea: implement micro-phase as a guarded experiment behind a per-tenant flag. Start with a low ticket budget and synthetic traffic that mimics small requests. Measure 99/99.9 pct token latency and tail throughput drop.
sam: Exactly. Canary on 10% tenants, parallel telemetry dashboard. Also need trace hooks to link micro-phase handoff events to kernel selection decisions in the runtime (so we can see whether micro-phases are causing suboptimal kernel choices).
max: One more: preemption behavior. If a regular big batch preempts GPU, micro-phase must be able to fast-fail or re-enqueue without causing double-count of tickets. Handshake protocol: `token->started->commit/abort` events. Tickets reclaimed on abort.
ogla: Do we need a minimum batch size for micro-phases? If you fire single-request micro-phases all the time you lose packing. Maybe set a lower bound (e.g., 2 requests or total tokens >= X) unless latency SLO forces 1-request cases.
sam: I'd make threshold configurable per-tenant and SLO-driven. Default to optimistic pack: attempt up to 4 requests or 64 tokens, whichever hits first, else flush at timeout.
jia: Sounds reasonable. Telemetry hooks: per-phase pack size histogram, per-tenant ticket exhaustion rate, micro-phase to regular-batch fallback ratio.
max: Implementation concern: concurrency of micro-phase coordinator + main batcher. Try to reuse the existing batch assembly codepaths to avoid duplication. Micro-phase coordinator should produce the same Batch object type, then hand it over.
sam: Good note — keep the handoff interface minimal: Batch { requests[], meta{phase_id,is_prefetch} } and an idempotent `accept_batch(batch)` call. That keeps runtime changes minimal.
ogla: Backward compat: if runtime doesn't support micro-phase meta, coordinator must detect and degrade to regular enqueue.
infra-bot: reminder: add feature flag + metric gating + kill-switch endpoints to incident playbook.
jia: Minor nit: naming — 'mini-phased' vs 'micro-phase' vs 'phased batcher' — pick one and be consistent in code. I vote `micro_phase` as field names.
sam: Agreed, use `micro_phase` prefix in APIs and metrics (`micro_phase.*`). I'll open a tiny RFC PR with diagrams and the handoff proto sketch. Thanks for the quick sanity checks.
max: SGTM. If PR includes a simple state machine (ticket lifecycle + handoff) I'll review.
ogla: Add a short checklist for KV eviction interactions and telemetry. I can pair-review that section.
infra-bot: logged: ticket 20432 created for telemetry dashboard.
sam: Thanks all — will post the PR link in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
